carousel-15.label: Relationships
lines: 5 ancient lines on who to let close.
“When friendship is settled, you must trust; before friendship is formed, you must pass judgment.”
Judge slowly. Then trust fully. Most of us do it backwards.
“Without friends no one would choose to live, though he had all other goods.”
Money, gym, status. None of it replaces three men who'd pick up at 3am.
You become the people you let close. Choose like it matters.
“When you wish to delight yourself, think of the virtues of those who live with you.”
Tonight, name one good thing about each person at your table.
When someone wrongs you, remember: they did what seemed right to them.
Understanding them isn't excusing them. It's refusing to carry their mistake.

carousel-22.label: Utilities
lines: 3 Stoic habits psychology tested 2,000 years later.

carousel-23.label: 1 · Name the judgment
lines: “If you are pained by any external thing, it is not this thing that disturbs you, but your own judgement about it.”
Modern name: cognitive reappraisal. Albert Ellis, a founder of CBT, credited Epictetus.

carousel-24.label: 2 · Review the day
lines: “I conceal nothing from myself, I omit nothing.”
Modern cousin: expressive writing. Writing honestly about hard days was linked to fewer health visits (Pennebaker & Beall, 1986).

carousel-25.label: 3 · Rehearse the moment
lines: “I will now go bathe, and keep my own mind in a state conformable to nature.”
Modern name: if-then plans. A review of 94 studies found they clearly improve follow-through (Gollwitzer & Sheeran, 2006).
